_about: The BackPorch backfill: existing SparkPoint events, stories, and news as porch posts, dated when they happened. Read and edit freely, then run `npm run porch:backfill` (preview) and `npm run porch:backfill -- --apply` (writes). Re-running updates posts by slug; it never duplicates them. `image.src` and block `src` are files in this repo; the script resizes and uploads them to porch-media. Pinned posts are written last, in list order, so the last one here leads. A post with "status": "draft" is written as a draft (no date needed): it waits in the editor at /internal/backporch until someone publishes it.

posts.title: Helene: One Year of Healing
posts.summary: A community tribute film made from interviews with more than 140 residents across Transylvania County, a year after Hurricane Helene.

image.alt: An audience fills an open-air auditorium as a resident's story plays on the big screen at Helene: One Year of Healing.

blocks.text:
In the year after Hurricane Helene, SparkPoint set out to listen. Our team interviewed more than 140 residents, volunteers, partners, and community leaders with one question: what has this year been like for you?

What came back was not one story but many: loss and exhaustion, generosity and resilience, and neighbors who kept showing up long after the lights came back on. This film is a tribute to those voices, and a reminder that healing happens together.

posts.title: Echoes from the Community, Week 5
posts.summary: As the new year begins, echoes from across Transylvania County invite us to treat connection as something we build every day.

image.alt: Echoes from the Community, SparkPoint's column of residents' stories.

blocks.text: Neighbors from Brevard, Rosman, Cedar Mountain, Pisgah Forest, Connestee Falls, Little River, and Schenck Job Corps have shared their stories. Some feel deeply connected; others feel isolated or unheard. Together they describe a community that values connection, and is still learning to practice it.
When was the last time you felt genuinely connected to someone, and why did it happen?

posts.title: When neighbors become leaders
posts.summary: Inside the first Community Connectors gathering, where SparkPoint, FWRD, and the American Red Cross listened to residents, and connectors stepped up to lead.

posts.title: Keep the conversation moving
posts.summary: October 1 attendees: join the virtual post-convening session on Thursday, November 5, at 10 a.m., on Zoom.

image.alt: Convening attendees in conversation across a table at Deerwoode Reserve.

blocks.text:
If you joined us on October 1, this is your invitation back. The WNC Regional Rural Health Virtual Post-Convening Session is a chance to reconnect with other rural health stakeholders and carry forward the conversations and partnerships that started at Deerwoode Reserve.

You'll hear about upcoming events, opportunities, and resources from the North Carolina Rural Health Association, the NC DHHS Office of Rural Health, Impact Health, and the WNC Health Policy Initiative.

posts.title: Welcome to the BackPorch
posts.summary: We made a place on our own website to share what's happening at SparkPoint: gatherings, stories, and the times we could use a hand. Come sit a while.

image.alt: A Community Connectors participant speaks with neighbors in a listening circle.

blocks.text:
Around here, a lot of the real news gets shared on somebody's back porch. A neighbor stops by, someone pours the coffee, and before long you know who's doing what and who could use a hand.

We wanted SparkPoint to have a place like that, so we made one, right here on our own website.

This is where we'll share what's going on: gatherings coming up, stories from neighbors, what we're learning, and the times we need your help. It all lands here first. You don't need an account or an app to read it, and you don't have to hope a social media feed decides to show it to you.

To get things started, we've brought some of the past year onto the porch, from Helene: One Year of Healing to the full house at Deerwoode Reserve on October 1. Have a look around.

You'll mostly hear from Jeff and Maggie here. And if you know of something that belongs on the porch, whether it's a gathering, a story, or a neighbor worth knowing, tell us. That's what a porch is for.
